subject: Sterile update transport & ephemeral key protocol — EdgeCloud pilot
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Liam Barnes <liam@edgecloud.io>, EdgeCloud Ops <ops@edgecloud.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 08:13:00 -0700
Subject: Sterile update transport & ephemeral key protocol — EdgeCloud pilot

Hi Liam / EdgeCloud Ops team,

Following up from last week's onboarding call — we want to lock down the sterile (air-gapped) update flow for the pilot sites you specified. Attached is a draft signed-manifest (redwood_signed-manifest_v2.json) and a strawman protocol for ephemeral key handling during transit. High-level asks: 

- Confirm acceptance criteria for on-site operator handshake (operator-acceptance-form_v1.pdf attached).
- Confirm whether CloudTransit can support double-blind sealing (tamper-evident envelope + courier seal) and provide chain-of-custody events (pickup, handoff, arrival).
- Agree on the signing-key rotation window (we propose ephemeral keys per delivery batch, rotated weekly).

Notes in the attached manifest include: signed artifact checksum (sha256), required operator identity attributes (name, badge id, PGP fingerprint), and minimal on-site verification steps that do NOT require internet access.

If EdgeCloud can accept the manifest as-is, we will prepare a DocuSign envelope for acceptance and schedule an on-call operator training 48-72 hours prior to the first shipment.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_signed-manifest_v2.json (signed JSON manifest, 12 KB), operator-acceptance-form_v1.pdf (fillable, 1 page)

From: Liam Barnes <liam@edgecloud.io>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, EdgeCloud Ops <ops@edgecloud.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sterile update transport & ephemeral key protocol — EdgeCloud pilot

Camila, thanks for the clear doc. A few clarifying questions from our side: 

1) Ephemeral key rotation: when you say "rotated weekly", do you mean a new signing key pair generated and used only for that week's batch, and then retired permanently afterward? That has implications for our courier partner and HSM usage.
2) Operator verification: our ops team prefers a short human-readable checklist on the courier manifest for the operator to initial. Can we add a 3-item checklist (visual seal OK, serial matches manifest, operator badge scanned)?
3) Chain-of-custody events: CloudTransit can provide pickup and handoff stamps and a scanned timestamp log, but they will not be able to attach photos by default for sealed shipments unless we add a courier workflow.

We are leaning toward accepting the manifest, but we need to confirm the key lifecycle. Attaching a sample transport SLA (transport-sla-sample.xlsx) and our preliminary comments inline.

Proposed next step: 30-minute sync on Fri; will Karthik and Priyom be available?

—Liam
Head of Infrastructure, EdgeCloud

Attachments: transport-sla-sample.xlsx (courier SLA sample, 3 sheets)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Liam Barnes <liam@edgecloud.io>, EdgeCloud Ops <ops@edgecloud.io>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sterile update transport & ephemeral key protocol — EdgeCloud pilot

Thanks Liam — quick responses inline and an action list.

1) Key lifecycle: Yes, ephemeral means we generate a signing key pair per batch in our HSM, sign the manifest, then rotate the key out of active use. Private keys are zeroized post-sign, public key included in the sealed manifest. We will keep an audit record of key fingerprints for 1 year (for incident investigation) but private keys will not be retained beyond the minimal HSM export policy. If EdgeCloud needs a longer retention window we can negotiate.

2) Operator checklist: Agreed. We'll append a three-line initial block on the paper manifest (Visual seal intact / Serial matches manifest / Operator badge scanned). We will accept a photographed badge scan as optional post-acceptance but not required at site for the sealed flow.

3) CloudTransit photos: understood. If you can provide pickup/handoff stamps and a scanned timestamped PDF per shipment that suffices for our compliance reviewers.

Action items: 
- Priyom: draft an updated manifest template with operator checklist and public-key fingerprint included. (Priyom to deliver by EOD Thu.)
- Camila: prepare DocuSign envelope once updated manifest landed.
- EdgeCloud/CloudTransit: confirm SLA table notes and whether additional courier workflow is billable.

Priyom — can you attach the operator acceptance form draft to this thread when ready?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Deployment Security
Redwood Inference

From: CloudTransit Logistics <logistics@cloudtransit.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>, Liam Barnes <liam@edgecloud.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Sep 2026 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Sterile shipment capabilities and sample manifest

---------- Forwarded message ----------
From: CloudTransit Ops <ops@cloudtransit.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Sep 2026 14:28:10 -0700
Subject: Sterile shipment capabilities and sample manifest
To: logistics@cloudtransit.com

Hi team, attaching our pickup/arrival stamp sample and courier checklist. We can support double-blind sealing and provide a signed PDF stamp per handoff. Photos are available as an add-on. Estimated per-shipment uplift for photo-proofing: $150.

Attachments: cloudtransit_pickup-stamp.pdf, courier-checklist-example.txt

—CloudTransit Ops

Notes to Redwood/EdgeCloud: we can align to the key rotation window but recommend a 72-hour window for key generation-to-shipment to allow for QA and HSM ops. We can accommodate a weekly cadence if Redwood generates keys on Monday morning and schedules shipments later in the week.

Attachments: cloudtransit_pickup-stamp.pdf (stamp example), courier-checklist-example.txt (text checklist)

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Liam Barnes <liam@edgecloud.io>, EdgeCloud Ops <ops@edgecloud.io>, CloudTransit Logistics <logistics@cloudtransit.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sterile update transport & ephemeral key protocol — EdgeCloud pilot

All — thanks for the quick turnaround and clarifications. Agreed summary and next steps below: 

Summary decisions: 
- Key lifecycle: Redwood will generate ephemeral signing keys per batch in our HSM, sign the manifest, zeroize private keys post-sign, retain fingerprints for 1 year.
- Operator checklist: 3-item initial block added to manifest; operator-acceptance-form_v1.pdf updated and attached.
- Courier: CloudTransit will provide pickup/handoff stamps as PDF and can optionally provide photo proof as a paid add-on.

Next steps: 
- Priyom: please attach the updated manifest and the operator-acceptance-form (final) to this thread by EOD Tue (2026-09-21).
- EdgeCloud: confirm whether you want photo-proof enabled for the pilot (Liam to reply).
- Camila/Marissa: I'll prepare the DocuSign envelope and share link once Priyom uploads final manifest. Target signature window: 72 hours before first shipment.

Proposed call: Wed 2026-09-22 09:00 PT (30 min) — calendar invite to follow.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: operator-acceptance-form_v1_final.pdf (fillable final form), signing-key-rotation-diagram.png (workflow diagram)
